title: Employee Benefits Policy
text:
New employees have 30 days from their
employment start date to enroll in benefits.

Available benefits include medical insurance,
dental insurance, vision coverage, and
retirement savings plans.

title: Employee Benefits Policy
text:
Employees who need assistance with benefits
enrollment should contact the People Operations
team.

The People Operations team can provide
information about enrollment deadlines and
available plans.

title: Legacy Benefits Enrollment Policy
text:
This is an outdated policy document retained for evaluation purposes.

The historical enrollment rule stated that new employees had 60 days from their employment start date to enroll in benefits.

This document is not the current source of benefits policy.

title: Legacy Benefits Enrollment Policy
text: Employees were historically instructed to contact the Benefits Administration team for enrollment questions.

title: Benefits Enrollment Update - Test Fixture
text:
This is a deliberately conflicting test document.

It states that new employees have 45 days from their employment start date to enroll in benefits.

The existing Employee Benefits Policy states a different enrollment deadline.

This document is intended to test whether the assistant detects conflicting policy sources rather than selecting one answer without qualification.

title: Benefits Enrollment Update - Test Fixture
text: Employees should contact People Operations when they encounter conflicting benefits information.

title: Workplace Code of Conduct
text:
Employees are expected to treat coworkers with professionalism and respect.

The company does not tolerate harassment, discrimination, intimidation, or retaliation in the workplace.

title: Workplace Code of Conduct
text:
Employees who experience or witness inappropriate workplace conduct may report their concerns to People Operations.

Employees may also use the company's designated reporting channels.

title: Workplace Code of Conduct
text: Reports involving workplace conduct should be handled carefully. Employees should avoid sharing sensitive details with people who are not involved in handling the concern.

title: Workplace Code of Conduct
text: Employees who believe they are in immediate danger should contact appropriate emergency services.

title: Equipment Policy
text: Employees who need a laptop, monitor, keyboard, or other standard work equipment should submit a request through the IT support portal.

title: Equipment Policy
text: Equipment requests are reviewed by the IT department. Additional approval may be required for specialized or nonstandard equipment.

title: Equipment Policy
text: Employees should report damaged or malfunctioning company equipment to IT as soon as possible. Employees should not attempt unauthorized hardware repairs.

title: Business Expense Policy
text:
Employees may request reimbursement for reasonable business expenses incurred while performing approved work activities.

Examples include approved business travel, required work supplies, and authorized business meals.

title: Business Expense Policy
text:
Employees must submit expense reports through the company's expense system.

Each submission should include the transaction date, amount, business purpose, and supporting receipt when available.

title: Business Expense Policy
text: Managers review submitted expenses for business purpose and policy compliance. Additional review may be required for unusual or high-value expenses.

title: Business Expense Policy
text: Employees with questions about reimbursement status should contact the Finance department.

title: Company Holiday Policy
text:
The company publishes its observed holiday schedule before the beginning of each calendar year.

Employees should consult the official company holiday calendar for specific dates.

title: Company Holiday Policy
text: Some departments may require staffing coverage during observed holidays. Managers are responsible for coordinating coverage with their teams.

title: Company Holiday Policy
text: Employees who have questions about holiday scheduling should contact People Operations.

title: Manager Guidance
text:
Managers should document employee performance concerns
and follow the company's established review process.

title: Manager Guidance
text:
Managers are responsible for reviewing team PTO requests
and coordinating staffing coverage.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
New employees should review their welcome materials and confirm that they can access the company's required systems.

Employees should contact their manager if they have not received their initial schedule or onboarding instructions.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
New employees may need access to email, collaboration tools, internal documentation, and role-specific applications.

Access requests should be submitted through the appropriate IT process. Managers are responsible for identifying the systems required for each employee's role.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
New employees should complete assigned orientation and security training.

Training assignments may vary depending on the employee's department and responsibilities.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
Managers should introduce new employees to their team and explain the employee's initial responsibilities.

Managers should identify a colleague who can help answer routine questions during the employee's first weeks.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
Managers should schedule an initial check-in during the employee's first week.

The discussion should cover access to required tools, initial responsibilities, and any obstacles affecting the employee's ability to begin work.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
Managers should review the employee's progress during the first month.

The conversation may cover training progress, role expectations, and questions about team processes.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
Employees who need help with onboarding should first contact their manager.

Questions involving account access or technical problems should be directed to IT support.

Questions about benefits, employment policies, or workplace procedures should be directed to People Operations.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
Managers should confirm that required onboarding activities have been completed.

Employees should follow instructions provided by their department for submitting required onboarding documentation.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
Remote employees receive onboarding instructions electronically.

Managers should confirm that remote employees can access required systems and know how to contact their team.

title: New Employee Onboarding Policy
text:
Employees may provide feedback about their onboarding experience to People Operations.

Feedback can identify missing documentation, access problems, or areas where instructions could be clearer.

title: Paid Time Off Policy
text:
Full-time employees receive 20 days of paid
time off annually.

PTO accrues monthly throughout the calendar
year. Employees may request time off through
the company's HR portal.

title: Paid Time Off Policy
text:
Employees should submit PTO requests at least
two weeks before their intended leave.

Managers are responsible for reviewing requests
within three business days.

Approval depends on staffing requirements
and business operations.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees may request remote work arrangements through their manager. Approval depends on job responsibilities, team needs, and operational requirements.

title: Remote Work Policy
text:
Employees working remotely are expected to remain available during their agreed working hours and attend scheduled team meetings.

Employees must protect company information when working outside the office. Confidential documents should not be left visible to unauthorized individuals.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees should contact IT for assistance with company-issued equipment used for remote work.

title: Security Awareness Training Policy
text:
Employees must complete security awareness training assigned by the company.

Training may cover phishing, password protection, safe handling of company information, and reporting suspicious activity.

title: Security Awareness Training Policy
text:
Employees who receive a suspicious email should report it using the company's designated security reporting process.

Employees should avoid opening unexpected attachments or entering credentials into unfamiliar websites.

title: Security Awareness Training Policy
text: Employees who cannot access assigned training should contact IT support.

title: Business Travel Policy
text:
Employees must receive manager approval before arranging business travel.

Travel requests should explain the business purpose, destination, expected dates, and estimated expenses.

title: Business Travel Policy
text: Employees should follow company travel procedures when booking transportation and accommodations.

title: Business Travel Policy
text:
Approved business travel expenses may be submitted through the company's expense system.

Employees should retain receipts and provide the business purpose for submitted expenses.

title: Business Travel Policy
text: Employees with questions about travel approval should contact their manager. Questions about reimbursement should be directed to Finance.
